final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor supplied no genuinely new admissible evidence; the response reframed the same record more narrowly and made concessions that are consistent with the initial concerns. That reframing is important, but it is not itself evidence. The strongest supportable interpretation of the current record is that aggregate readiness and lack of severity-one rehearsal incidents support general launch readiness, while the policy text still leaves an unresolved compliance condition for this specific exposed weakness. The distinction matters: a caveated certification theory could potentially support compliant_with_caveats if the record showed that disclosure-based certification is explicitly allowed and actually implemented in final launch materials, or that approved risk acceptance or scope exclusion covers the exposure. On the record available to this role, none of those predicates is proven. Because the key condition remains unverified, the claim that certification is compliant and evidentially supportable remains suspicious rather than compliant_with_caveats.
remaining_concerns: No new admissible evidence was provided showing final launch materials actually contain the required explicit disclosure of the legal-intake privilege-routing limitation.
The legal intake triage segment remains below target on privilege-sensitive routing and remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
The available policy text states that rollout controls and monitoring mitigate only if the affected use case is excluded or reviewed risk acceptance exists; neither condition is evidenced here.
The risk-acceptance draft remains incomplete and does not cover the legal intake triage exposure.

The Actor's narrowed position is more disciplined than the original broader claim, but it still depends on an unproven compliance predicate: actual disclosure in final launch materials or some other policy-permitted sign-off artifact.
